profile.headline: Software Engineer | React, TypeScript, C#/.NET | Network Automation & Enterprise Tooling
profile.summary: Full-stack software engineer with 4+ years of experience building and modernizing enterprise web applications in React, TypeScript, and C#/.NET. At Citi, I build network automation services that replace manual operational workflows for infrastructure engineers — designing React front ends and C#/.NET backends for provisioning, decommissioning, and access control systems. On top of core delivery, I identify systemic inefficiencies in the development process itself and ship solutions: reusable component architectures, testing infrastructure, and developer tooling that reduce friction across the team. I integrate AI tooling (Copilot, Claude) into daily workflows for code generation, spec-driven development, and automated PR review.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Build and ship full-stack network automation services (React/TypeScript, C#/.NET) that replace manual operational workflows for infrastructure engineers — including decommissioning pipelines, access control provisioning, and load balancer management.

Beyond core delivery, I focus on reducing friction across the development process:

Identified ~400 lines of duplicated code across admin tools and consolidated it into a single reusable React component, cutting new-tool build time from 2 days to 2 hours

Discovered a runaway retry loop in a background job worker that had silently generated 2M+ log entries — traced the root cause and drove remediation

Introduced Jest and React Testing Library on a previously untested legacy app; established CI coverage gates and team-wide testing conventions in one sprint
positions.insights: Skills: React · Web Applications · C# · RESTful WebServices · SQL / SSMS · JavaScript · .Net Framework / ASP.NET MVC

positions.title: UI Developer
positions.description:
In my role as a UI Developer at Bank of America, I was part of an Agile team focused on understanding, documenting, and presenting the workings of a proprietary software built with React with TypeScript. My responsibilities included:

● Participating in daily Agile standup meetings, discussing team progress, and identifying potential roadblocks.
● Observing standup meetings of a parallel team to gain a broader understanding of the project's scope and challenges.
● Engaging in "Knowledge Transfer" (KT) sessions, where the intricacies of the codebase were explained, including its architecture, functionality, and the rationale behind its design.
● Analyzing and debugging the codebase to understand its structure and functionality, using tools like Jira and Bitbucket for tracking changes and managing the codebase.
● Creating comprehensive technical documentation on various aspects of the software, managing and organizing these documents using SharePoint for easy access and reference by the team.
● Presenting the created documentation in meetings, facilitating knowledge sharing among the team and ensuring everyone was on the same page regarding the software's functionality.

This role, while not coding-intensive, allowed me to develop a deep understanding of a complex React with TypeScript codebase, Agile methodologies, and the use of tools like Jira, Bitbucket, and SharePoint in a large, structured corporate environment. It honed my skills in software analysis, technical documentation, and effective knowledge transfer within a team.

positions.title: Frontend Developer
positions.description:
At InnovA Technologies, I was a key contributor to the development of a complex auctioning platform and a comprehensive Product Inventory Management System (PIMS)/Content Management System (CMS). My primary focus was on the front end of the PIMS/CMS site, where I implemented CRUD operations across several domains including products, images, sales personnel, sales goals, and more.

● Participating in daily Agile standup meetings, discussing progress, identifying potential roadblocks, and setting daily goals.
● Writing code for 5-6 hours a day, focusing on creating and updating forms, building new pages/components, and integrating Redux and RESTful APIs from a .Net core backend.
● Occasionally working with the SQL database to understand the data structure and inform front-end development.
● Submitting code for review by peers and senior developers, as well as reviewing others' code to ensure quality and consistency.
● Using GitHub Desktop and DevOps for version control and story management.
● Continually improving the user experience by reconfiguring components, creating new components, adding features to pre-existing components, and fixing UI bugs.

This role allowed me to deepen my skills in React and JavaScript, Redux, RESTful APIs, and Agile methodologies. I also gained experience in code review processes and working closely with a SQL database. My contributions were recognized in my 90-day review, where I was noted for far exceeding expectations.

While the company was in a proof-of-concept state during my tenure, I played a significant role in shaping the user interface and functionality of the PIMS/CMS, setting the foundation for future development and success.

As a stocker, my duties included unloading pallets of product from a company truck that arrived weekly. After which, my coworkers and I would work through the night and the following morning distributing the product to the appropriate locations before the store reopened.

positions.description:
As a file clerk at The Frist Clinic of Nashville, I was part of a fast working, friendly, efficient team of individuals who were in charge of taking requests from Doctors and nurses alike, finding the charts or files they needed and providing them with said chart or file. 

Additional duties included, but were not limited to: Keeping the workplace tidy and organize, delivering mail and other time-sensitive parcels to the different departments of the Clinic, closing down the file room at the end of the night and, if time allowed, constructing any new chairs, desks, printers, etc. that were ordered for the office.

projects.title: Admin Dashboard
projects.description:
This project is a comprehensive and secure interface designed for managing the various aspects of its counterpart, the e-commerce platform. It's built using Next.js, a popular React framework that provides features like server-side rendering and static site generation, making the admin interface highly performant and SEO-friendly.

The primary functionality of the admin interface includes the ability to add, edit, and delete products. Each product has multiple properties such as title, description, price, and images. The interface is designed to make managing these properties as straightforward as possible, with forms for adding new products and intuitive options for editing existing ones.

In addition to product management, the admin interface also provides tools for order management. Administrators can view details of orders placed by customers, including the ordered products, customer information, and order status. This allows for efficient tracking and management of orders, ensuring a smooth shopping experience for customers.

The admin interface interacts with a MongoDB database for persistent data storage. This ensures that all product and order information is securely stored and readily available when needed. The use of MongoDB also allows for scalability, supporting a large number of products and orders.

Security is a key focus in the admin portion of the project. Access to the admin interface is restricted to authorized users only, preventing unauthorized access and potential misuse of the platform.

Overall, this project is designed to provide a smooth and efficient experience for administrators, making it easy to manage the e-commerce platform and ensure a high-quality shopping experience for customers.
